sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Swap · You will need · Steps · Done looks like · Common mistakes.

YOU WILL NEED
Main water shutoff valve location · Breaker box and breaker for unit · Garden hose · Floor drain · New water heater (spec: ASK OWNER) · New flex lines · Camera or phone for photo.

STEPS
1. Shut the water at the main valve. Do not rely on the small shutoff valve on the tank.
2. Kill the breaker for the water heater at the breaker box.
3. Connect a garden hose to the drain valve and run it to the floor drain. Open the valve and let it drain completely.
4. Disconnect the old flex lines and any other connections to the tank.
5. Remove the old water heater from its location.
6. Set the new water heater in place and connect new flex lines. Use new flex lines every time, even if old ones look intact.
7. Fill the tank by closing the drain valve and opening the main water shutoff.
8. Bleed air from the system at the closest faucet to the heater. Run until water flows clear.
9. Restore power by flipping the breaker back on.
10. Wait 20 minutes. Check all connections and the floor around the unit for leaks.
11. Take a photo of the new unit and any relevant connections. File it in the job record.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
New unit running, no water pooling on the floor after 20 minutes, air bled from the line, breaker on, photo taken and filed, old unit removed from site.

COMMON MISTAKES
1. Trusting the tank shutoff valve and skipping the main. Check: water still draining after you close the tank valve. If it is, you missed the main.
2. Forgetting to check and install an expansion tank if there is a check valve on the main line. Check: ask the homeowner or look at the main shutoff. If there is a check valve and no expansion tank on the existing line, flag this for the owner (ASK OWNER if this is a standard add-on charge).
3. Testing for leaks too early. Check: set a phone timer for 20 minutes after power on. Do not assume no drip at 2 minutes means no leak.
sop-from-memo.spoken: Water heater swap has three steps that matter: shut the main water and the breaker first, drain it, swap the tank with new flex lines. Wait 20 minutes after power, not 2, then check for leaks and take a photo. Guys forget the expansion tank if there is a check valve on the main. Say read the rest to hear everything else.
